mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint relationship between Team A's shots FOR (all-prior: 11.41, recent-5: 15.2) and goals FOR (all-prior: 1.18, recent-5: 2.2) alongside shots_on_target FOR (all-prior: 3.78, recent-5: 5.8). Measure whether the recent uplift in shots and shots_on_target co-moves proportionally with goals, or whether goals rise disproportionately relative to the shot increase — i.e., test the joint shots × shots_on_target × goals relationship rather than any single observable alone.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both shots FOR and shots_on_target FOR rise together in the recent window relative to the long-run baseline, goals FOR rises more than proportionally to the shot increase (super-linear co-movement), rather than remaining flat or rising only in proportion.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume has risen sharply in recent matches while its conversion rate (goals per shot) has not kept pace, suggesting a divergence between shot production and scoring efficiency. Jointly tracking Team A's shots FOR and goals FOR across the all-prior versus recent-5 windows reveals whether elevated shot counts translate into goals or represent a low-conversion regime.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint relationship across three distinct observables (shots, shots_on_target, goals) comparing their co-movement across two time windows. It cannot be reduced to any single observable versus one band; it tests whether the ratio of goals to shots changes as shot volume changes — a non-linear, multi-observable structure.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's shots FOR vs AGAINST (all-prior: 11.41 vs 11.78; recent-5: 15.2 vs 11.8), shots_on_target FOR vs AGAINST (all-prior: 3.78 vs 4.25; recent-5: 5.8 vs 4.6), and goals FOR vs AGAINST (all-prior: 1.18 vs 1.59; recent-5: 2.2 vs 1.6). The mechanism tests whether the cross-side asymmetry in shot-to-goal conversion (Team A converting shots at a different rate than opponents do against Team A) is a stable or regime-dependent feature.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: In the recent window, Team A's goals FOR rises relative to shots FOR (improving conversion) while goals AGAINST remains stable despite shots AGAINST falling — indicating an asymmetric cross-side conversion pattern that diverges from the long-run baseline.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A structurally concedes more shots and shots_on_target than it produces over its full history, yet its recent-5 goal output has risen while goals conceded remain stable. This asymmetry between Team A's offensive shot-to-goal conversion and its defensive shot-against-to-goal-against conversion — measured jointly — may indicate a regime where Team A scores more efficiently than it defends, despite being outshot.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric cross-observable relationship across both sides simultaneously (FOR and AGAINST for shots, shots_on_target, and goals), requiring a joint four-variable structure. It cannot be reduced to a single observable's FOR vs AGAINST mirror or a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's possession FOR (all-prior vs recent-5 shift), Team B's possession FOR (stable high), and both teams' corner_kicks and fouls FOR/AGAINST. The mechanism asks: when Team A's possession approaches parity with Team B's (as in recent-5), does the corner-kick differential and foul differential between the two sides compress or diverge relative to what each team's individual possession baseline predicts?
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: As Team A's possession rises toward parity with Team B, the corner-kick differential between the two sides compresses (Team A corners FOR rises, Team B corners AGAINST rises), and the foul differential narrows — a joint non-linear response across three observables that is not captured by any single observable's own baseline.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's possession share has shifted substantially in recent matches (all-prior: 40.3%, recent-5: 48.4%) while Team B consistently holds above-average possession (all-prior: 52.4%, recent-5: 55.2%). The joint possession profiles of both teams in the same match create a contested possession dynamic distinct from either team's individual baseline. This mechanism tests whether the joint possession balance between a low-possession team (Team A historically) and a high-possession team (Team B) is associated with a different corner-kick and foul distribution than either team's individual possession baseline would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly tracking possession FOR for both teams simultaneously alongside corner_kicks and fouls, testing a three-observable interaction. It is not reducible to one observable with one band; it tests how the balance of two teams' possession levels jointly predicts distributional outcomes in two other observables.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on Team B's goals FOR in the first half versus second half, and Team A's goals AGAINST in the first half versus second half. The mechanism requires half-level resolution for both teams simultaneously, testing whether the cross-team first-half goal rate is elevated relative to the second-half rate in a way that neither team's full-match average captures.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The joint first-half goal rate (Team B scoring + Team A conceding) is elevated relative to the second-half joint rate, and this half-level asymmetry is more pronounced than either team's individual full-match goal average would suggest — i.e., the first half is disproportionately goal-rich for this specific matchup structure.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B scores heavily in the first half (goals FOR 1H: 0.897) relative to the second half (goals FOR 2H: 1.0 over full match minus 1H), while Team A concedes more in the first half (goals AGAINST 1H: 0.809) than the second half (goals AGAINST 2H: 0.779). Jointly, this creates a within-match half-level asymmetry where Team B's first-half goal production meets Team A's first-half defensive vulnerability — a cross-team, cross-half joint structure. The mechanism tests whether the joint first-half goal environment (Team B's 1H scoring rate combined with Team A's 1H concession rate) exceeds what either team's full-match baseline would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a within-match half-level split applied jointly across both teams' asymmetric observables (Team B's 1H scoring profile combined with Team A's 1H defensive profile). It requires two-team, two-half conditioning simultaneously, which is not reducible to a single observable's half split or a single team's half-level average.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's fouls FOR (all-prior vs recent-5 decline) and Team B's fouls FOR (all-prior vs recent-5 rise), alongside both teams' yellow_cards FOR and cards_2h FOR. The mechanism tests whether the joint foul-rate regime (which team is currently the higher-fouling side) predicts the direction of yellow-card and second-half card asymmetry between the two teams.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's recent foul rate falls below Team B's recent foul rate (a crossover from the long-run baseline), Team A's yellow cards FOR and cards_2h FOR are suppressed relative to Team B's, and this asymmetry is more pronounced in the second half — a joint three-observable, two-team, within-match-period structure.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's fouls FOR have dropped sharply in recent matches (all-prior: 12.28, recent-5: 9.2) while Team B's fouls FOR have risen slightly (all-prior: 10.19, recent-5: 11.0). Jointly, this creates a foul-rate regime shift where the historically higher-fouling team (Team A) is now fouling less than its opponent. The mechanism tests whether this joint foul-rate crossover — where Team A's recent foul rate falls below Team B's recent foul rate — is associated with a corresponding shift in yellow-card and second-half card distributions, given that cards_2h and yellow_cards are also tracked for both teams.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly tracking fouls, yellow_cards, and cards_2h across both teams simultaneously, conditioning on a regime crossover (which team is currently the higher-fouling side) rather than any single team's foul rate in isolation. It involves two distinct observables (fouls and cards) across two teams with a within-match period dimension (cards_2h), which is not reducible to any single observable with one band.
